entries.description:
SQL written by hand, on the session's own database connection — the one hatch past the engine. What runs here is not seen by the access policy, the row-level restrictions or the register rules, so it is allowed only to a user with the Data administration right; anyone else gets an access error at the first call.

It runs where the script runs, on the server, on the connection the session's queries and writes use, and so inside their transaction. The SQL is the database's own dialect over the physical tables, whose names are the engine's, not the configuration's: to read the configuration's data, the query language (Query) is the road; this one is for the administrator's work the engine has no verb for.

Values never go into the SQL text. A statement that takes values is prepared with `?` in their places (PrepareStatement) and given them with SetParam — the database receives them as bound parameters.

Prepares ONE statement whose values are written as `?` and given afterwards with SetParam, by position from 1. The way to run SQL with values in it: they reach the database as bound parameters, so a quote or a per cent sign in a value is just a character. A text the database refuses raises with its message.
entries.parameters: sql — one statement, with `?` where each value goes.

entries.description:
Runs SQL that returns no rows — INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, a change of the schema. Several statements separated by `;` run one after another. The text is sent as it is, so it must carry no values from outside: a statement with values goes through PrepareStatement. A SELECT belongs to RunQueryWithResults; some databases refuse it here. A failing statement raises with the database's message.

The number it answers is what the driver reports, and some report 0 here whatever was touched; for a reliable count of changed rows, run the statement prepared.
entries.parameters: sql — the statement(s), with no values from outside in them.
entries.return_descr: Number — as the driver reports it.

entries.description: Runs one SELECT and answers its rows, to be walked with Next. Like RunQuery, the text goes as it is: a SELECT that compares with a value from outside is prepared instead (PrepareStatement, then the statement's RunQueryWithResults). A text the database refuses raises with its message.
entries.parameters: sql — one SELECT, with no values from outside in it.

entries.description:
One SQL statement, prepared once, with `?` in the places of its values. SetParam gives each value by position; RunQuery or RunQueryWithResults runs it, and it can be run again with other values without being prepared again. Made only by DatabaseLayer.PrepareStatement.

A result set the statement gave is read while the statement is still held: keep the statement's variable until the rows have been walked, and let the result set go first.

Gives the value for the `?` at `position`, counted from 1 in the order the question marks stand in the text. A Boolean, a Number, a Date and a String are bound as they are; any other value — Undefined, Null, a reference — is bound as NULL. Position 0, or one past the last `?`, raises ("Index goes beyond statement").
entries.parameters:
position — the `?`'s number, from 1.
value — a Boolean, Number, Date or String; anything else is NULL.

entries.description: Runs the prepared statement — an INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE — with the values given so far, and answers how many rows it changed. Takes no arguments.
Runs the prepared SELECT with the values given so far and answers its rows. Takes no arguments. Keep the statement held while the rows are read.

The rows of a SELECT run by hand, read forward once. Next moves to a row; then each column reads as a property by the name the database gives it — the AS alias, in the case the database keeps it in. A boolean, number, date or string column reads as such; a NULL in such a column reads as its type's empty value — 0, an empty string — not as Null; a column of another kind (a binary one) reads Undefined. Read-only.

A column is read ON A ROW: before the first Next, and after the Next that answered False, reading one raises ("the result set stands on no row").

Moves to the next row — the first one on the first call — and answers True, or False when there are no more. Read fields only after Next() returns True: a column read before the first Next, or after the one that answered False, raises.
